note: Where design evidence comes from, and what each source can and cannot answer. `reach` is the honest field: bundlebox never scrapes a site that forbids it and never pretends a JS-rendered gallery is an API. `web` means hand the plan to an agent holding a web tool; `http` means bb can GET it itself; `manual` means a human exports it.

kinds.shots: single static frames, art-directed, no states
kinds.flows: real product screens in sequence, with states
kinds.systems: published design systems and platform guidelines
kinds.patterns: installable UI patterns an agent can fetch as skills, with code
kinds.tooling: tools that verify, measure or compress the work rather than inspire it

providers.name: Dribbble
providers.beware: A shot is a poster, not a product. No empty state, no error, no long string, no 300-row list. Copying a shot is how a UI becomes pretty and unusable.
providers.license: All rights reserved by each author. Reference and describe; never copy assets or markup.

providers.name: Behance
providers.beware: Case studies are written to win the client, not to report the result. Read the decisions, discount the outcomes.
providers.license: All rights reserved by each author.

providers.name: Mobbin
providers.beware: The antidote to shots. Prefer this over Dribbble whenever the question is how something behaves rather than how it looks.
providers.license: Subscription; screenshots of third-party apps. Reference only.

providers.name: Awwwards
gives: typographic scale at the top end
providers.beware: Selected for jury appeal. Strong on ambition, weak on the boring screens that carry a product.
providers.license: All rights reserved by each studio.

providers.name: Godly
providers.beware: Curated to a single taste. Sampling only from here produces a house style.
providers.license: All rights reserved by each studio.

providers.name: Land-book
providers.beware: Marketing pages only. Says nothing about an app's interior.
providers.license: All rights reserved by each studio.

providers.name: SiteInspire
providers.beware: Skews editorial and agency. Few dense tools.
providers.license: All rights reserved by each studio.

providers.name: Laws of UX
gives: Fitts, Hick, Miller, Jakob, Doherty, Tesler, von Restorff, peak-end, serial position, Gestalt
providers.beware: Summaries. Each card names the original paper; cite the paper when a rule is contested.
providers.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (Jon Yablonski). Attribute.

providers.name: Nielsen Norman Group
providers.beware: The strongest evidence in this list. When a shot and an NN/g study disagree, the study wins.
providers.license: Articles free to read; all rights reserved. Cite by URL.

providers.name: Interaction Design Foundation
providers.beware: Encyclopaedic and uneven. Good for orientation, weak as a final citation.
providers.license: Mixed; much is open literature. Cite by URL.

providers.name: Material Design 3
providers.beware: Adopting M3 wholesale is one of the fastest routes to a generic UI. Take the STRUCTURE (state layers, token roles), refuse the SKIN.
providers.license: Apache 2.0 for the spec text and reference code.

providers.name: Apple Human Interface Guidelines
providers.beware: Normative on Apple platforms, advisory elsewhere.
providers.license: Apple. Cite by URL.

providers.name: Refactoring UI
gives: hierarchy by weight and colour not size
spacing scales that are not linear
providers.beware: Paid book. Its defaults became Tailwind's defaults, which is exactly the look this toolkit flags as generic. Use the reasoning, not the swatches.
providers.license: Paid. Do not reproduce.

providers.name: Typewolf
gives: what is current versus what is tired
providers.beware: The single highest-leverage source for escaping a generic look: typeface choice moves more than colour.
providers.license: All rights reserved. Reference only.

providers.name: Fonts In Use
gives: typefaces with provenance and industry context
providers.beware: Print-heavy. Check licensing and webfont availability before committing.
providers.license: Editorial; images credited. Reference only.

providers.name: Fontsource
gives: self-hostable open typefaces with a real JSON API
providers.beware: The one type source bb can query directly. Use it to verify a chosen face is actually shippable.
providers.license: Per-family open licences (OFL, Apache). Machine-readable.

providers.name: Huemint
gives: palettes generated against a layout rather than a wheel
providers.beware: Generated palettes still need a contrast pass. Nothing here is accessible by construction.
providers.license: Generated output is free to use.

providers.name: Motion
gives: durations that hold up on device
providers.beware: Library docs. Take the timing reasoning, not the API.
providers.license: MIT library; docs free to read.

providers.name: WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference
gives: normative contrast ratios, target sizes, focus visibility, motion preferences
providers.beware: Normative, not advisory. A rule here outranks every aesthetic source in this file.
providers.license: W3C Document Licence. Quote freely with attribution.

providers.name: UI Skills (ibelick)
gives: an MCP server exposing list_skills and get_skill
providers.beware: Patterns arrive as code, so they arrive with someone else's taste attached. Take the mechanism; re-token the surface against your own system or you have imported a second design language.
providers.license: MIT. Reusable, with attribution.
providers.use: npx ui-skills list --category motion · npx ui-skills get <skill>

providers.name: fwc-swiftui-skills (FloWritesCode)
gives: modern SwiftUI patterns as agent skills
providers.beware: Apple-platform idiom. Excellent where the target is SwiftUI, misleading where it is web or Flutter.
providers.license: See repository. Cite by URL.
providers.use: install as a coding-agent skill for Claude Code, Cursor or Codex

providers.name: anti-slop (dmmulroy)
gives: 20 Oxlint rules that reject low-evidence TypeScript patterns
providers.beware: The code-side sibling of this toolkit's ui-generic detector: same thesis, different surface. It says nothing about an interface, and ui-generic says nothing about a type assertion. Run both.
providers.license: MIT (one rule vendored from ESLint Stylistic, MIT).
providers.use: vendor src/ into the repo and register in oxlint.config.ts

providers.name: Reticle
gives: runtime verdicts from inside a running app: network, console, state, DOM, routing
pass / fail / couldn't tell, with file:line
MCP integration and deterministic flow replay
providers.beware: This is the answer to every UNKNOWN `bb designlabs check` prints. A declared state that renders identically to rest is invisible to a parse and obvious to a runtime observer. Localhost only; nothing leaves the machine.
providers.license: Open source. See repository.
providers.use: npx @reticlehq/server init, then drive the flow and read the verdict

providers.name: Caliper
gives: success rate, pass@k and pass^k over repeated runs
tokens and wall clock per attempt
ablation: what a skill contributes versus its absence
providers.beware: The honest way to claim a prompt or a skill works. One successful run is an anecdote; `--k 3` is a measurement. It costs real tokens, unlike everything else in this file.
providers.license: Open source. See repository.

providers.name: Chisle
gives: output-side compression: terse prose, YAGNI-first code, scrubbed and elided tool output
a decision ladder before code is written
a measured 44% of a bare model's output tokens over 20 tasks
providers.beware: Compresses what the model WRITES; bundlebox compresses what it READS. The two do not overlap and the savings compound. Its ~1.6k-token ruleset is charged once per session and belongs in the overhead term of any budget you quote.
providers.license: See repository.

providers.name: Ouroboros
gives: an immutable spec as the unit of work
a three-stage gate: mechanical, semantic, consensus
stops on ontology convergence rather than on a turn count
providers.beware: The workflow shape a storybook prompt should follow. Its mechanical gate is the cheap one and should run first; consensus is the expensive one and should run last, on what survived.
providers.license: Open source. See repository.
providers.use: ooo interview · ooo run · ooo auto
